candidates.title: Reliable AI at Scale: Lessons from Dataiku & Mistral AI, mar. 27 oct. 2026, 18:30 | Meetup
candidates.snippet:
Détails Join us on October 27th at 6:30 pm at our Paris office to explore what it really takes to make AI work in the real world. Maxime Appé and Thierry Gengler from Dataiku will show how to keep autonomous LLM agents under control without sacrificing their flexibility. Then Harizo Rajaona from Mistral AI will take us behind the scenes of serving a text-to-speech model at scale, one audio frame at a time. 6:30 – 7:15 pm | Maxime Appé, Technical Product Manager, and Thierry Gengler, Engineering Manager, Dataiku Taming Rogue LLMs:

7:15 – 8:00 pm | Harizo Rajaona, Software Engineer, Mistral AI Deploying and Running a TTS Model: The Fun Part Text-to-speech (TTS) models have improved dramatically in recent years, driven by the rise of Transformer architectures. Training one might sound like the hard part, but wait until you have to serve it at scale! TTS comes with its own set of challenges: tokenizing audio frames without information loss, combining a decoder with flow-matching transformers, and handling real-time streaming. This talk walks through these challenges and the engineering choices involved in building and serving Voxtral TTS, proving that making GPUs actually talk is hard but a lot of fun! The talks will be followed by open discussion and networking. Come ready to ask questions.

candidates.title: A quantum and AI hackathon for defence, at the Grand Palais in December
candidates.snippet:
# A quantum and AI hackathon for defence, at the Grand Palais in December
The French Defence Innovation Agency and Artefact bring engineering students together on 2 to 4 December 2026, with teams selected in October and November.
![](/logos/france2030.svg)
The Defence Innovation Agency (AID) and Artefact organise a Quantum Defence Hackathon from 2 to 4 December 2026 at the Grand Palais in Paris, during the Adopt AI Summit. Engineering students work in teams of four to eight on quantum computing and artificial intelligence applications for defence.

- Hackathon from 2 to 4 December 2026 at the Grand Palais, 10 avenue des Champs-Élysées, Paris, within the Adopt AI Summit; awards ceremony at the end.
- Organised by the Defence Innovation Agency (AID) and Artefact; Thales is announced as a sponsor.
- Aimed at engineering students, in teams of four to eight; more than 100 participants and over ten teams expected; focus on quantum computing and AI applications for defence.
- Timeline: call for ideas launched on 16 June 2026 at France Quantum, team selection and preparatory work with mentors in October and November, then the three-day event.
The [Quantum Defence Hackathon](https://hackathons-artefactadoptai.agorize.com/fr/challenges/hackathon-quantique-defense?lang=en) takes place from 2 to 4 December 2026 at the Grand Palais in Paris, as part of the Adopt AI Summit. It is organised by the Defence Innovation Agency (AID), the innovation arm of the French armed forces ministry, together with Artefact.
The format is a three-day immersive challenge for engineering students, in teams of four to eight people, on quantum computing and artificial intelligence applications for defence. The organisers expect more than a hundred participants and over ten teams. The call for ideas was launched on 16 June 2026 at France Quantum; teams are selected and prepared with mentors in October and November, and the hackathon closes with an awards ceremony.
The event was relayed on LinkedIn by [Frédéric Barbaresco](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7501911676779261952/), who notes that Thales sponsors it and that it was presented by Xavier Grison of the Defence Innovation Agency.

candidates.title: "The Strength of Weak Signals" Open-Lab @UNESCO Futures Literacy Summit
candidates.snippet: research As part UNESCO Future Literacies Summit, LIID Future Lab and MJV Innovation host an open-lab session to explore the many facets and benefits of weak-signals research, whether from a future literacy, foresight, innovation, sustainability or Covid-19 crisis perspective. Weak signals detection and analysis is crucial to the art of foresight and can be a specially inclusive and responsive practice in high uncertainty contexts. It is however rarely discussed in depth. In that regard, the session will highlight a white paper on weak signals recently published by BNP Paribas Risk Innovation with other members of the Chief Innovation Officer Club of Paris such as Malakoff Humanis and Thalès Alenia Space (download white paper here). Guests: Danielle Winandy and Pauline Bantegnie (BNP Paribas Risk Innovation Office), Peter Poppe (BNP Paribas Risk Innovation Champion), Siham Harroussi (Malakoff Humanis) and Cédric Balty (Thales Alenia Space)

candidates.title: Thales ranked No.1 most attractive employer among engineering students in France in 2025
candidates.snippet:
Thales has secured the **top spot in the 2025 ranking of the most attractive employers for engineering students in France**, in a survey conducted by the Universum research institute. The survey covered 23,376 students, including 11,556 from engineering schools. Thales also ranked 4th among IT students.
Students notably praised the Group’s capacity for innovation and the wide range of career development opportunities it offers.

Last year, **Thales engaged with over 150,000 young people** through 600 events. In 2025, in France alone, **the Group expects to welcome more than 3,000 interns and apprentices in higher education, with around 25% going on to secure permanent or fixed-term roles**. Nearly 1,500 students in Year 10 and Year 11 will also be welcomed for short-term work experience across around 40 Thales sites in mainland France, helping to spark interest in science and technology careers.

candidates.title: Forum Icam Entreprises 2026: A Celebration of Networking and Innovation
candidates.snippet:
Entreprises Grands PartenairesIcam
31 Mar 2026
**The Forum Icam Entreprises 2026, held on Friday 27 March** at the Espace Champerret in Paris, was a resounding success! The Icam students from across our various campuses, along with the many companies in attendance — including our Major Partner companies — contributed greatly to this achievement. This 16th edition, powered by the enthusiasm and energy of everyone involved, confirmed that the Forum Icam Entreprises is **a place to connect, a place of opportunity, and a place where career paths take shape**.

Once again this year, conversations were lively and discoveries plentiful, with some outstanding opportunities on offer for our students: **internships, jobs, apprenticeships and volunteer missions.** Several activities made this edition memorable, including a **sophrology introductory workshop** to help students manage pre-interview stress, a **professional photo booth** for headshots, and a prize draw to win **work experience placements at participating industrial companies**.
The highlight of the day was the **Model Mania competition**, co-organised by AvenAo, Prodways Group and Dassault Systèmes. Students were challenged to model a 3D part in record time from a technical drawing using SOLIDWORKS software. Speed, technical skill and creativity were all on show in this hugely popular activity — the winning student completed the challenge in just 3 minutes!

Several conferences punctuated the day, organised by **the Icam Alumni association**, the **Délégation Catholique pour la Coopération** (DCC) — a longstanding partner that opens doors for Icam engineers to engage in international volunteering — and **Apec**.
Participants gained insight into **trends shaping the engineering sector** and identified the key skills needed to meet future challenges. A dedicated conference focused on **what recruiters are looking for in 2026**, featuring speakers including Cyrille Courtier, an Icam alumnus and HR Director at Moët-Hennessy and Dior.

candidates.title: Latest Mistral AI Summit Paris Highlights
candidates.snippet:
On May 28, 2026, Mistral AI packed Paris’s Le Carrousel du Louvre for its first-ever flagship event, [AI Now Summit](https://ainowsummit.com/). The one-day conference drew more than a hundred speakers across three tracks and a sponsor list that reads like a who’s who of European enterprise IT: Accenture, Microsoft, and SAP as platinum sponsors; Capgemini, NTT Data, Qualcomm, and TCS as gold; EY, NVIDIA, Reply, and Sentry as silver; and Equinix, Neo4j, Orange, Qdrant, and Snorkel rounding out the bronze tier. The message from the stage was consistent and blunt: Europe has a narrow window to build its own AI infrastructure, and the time to move from pilots to production deployments is now.
The summit’s tagline, “Own your AI transformation,” captured the shift in tone. This was a deployment conference aimed at teams in finance, defense, manufacturing, energy, and the public sector that are done experimenting and need to industrialize AI at scale. The three tracks reflected that directly: the Vision stage for executives, the Build stage for engineers moving from proof of concept to production, and the Act track of hands-on workshops and product deep dives. The venue choice itself, Le Carrousel du Louvre, signaled ambition: this was a full-scale industry conference designed to project Mistral as the anchor of European AI.

The summit opened with a keynote from Arthur Mensch, Mistral’s co-founder and CEO, who framed the event around a single urgency: Europe’s dependence on US-hosted AI infrastructure is a strategic liability, and the fix requires building native compute, models, and deployment pipelines. Mensch’s message, echoed across the day’s sessions, was that Europe has roughly two years to establish autonomous AI capability before the gap with US and Chinese players becomes structural rather than merely competitive. This two-year thesis, which Mensch has been repeating in interviews leading up to the conference, was the organizing idea behind every session on the agenda.
The agenda split cleanly by audience. The Vision stage featured sessions on scaling AI to support the energy transition, building citizen-centric AI systems for governments, and reinventing manufacturing with AI. The Build stage went deeper into the mechanics: autonomous AI workflows, scalable optimization, OCR at scale, and a session titled “Building your own model” that walked through open-source and custom training approaches. The Act track ran 20-minute partner workshops, live product demonstrations, and 45-minute Mistral deep dives combining enterprise use cases with hands-on technical sessions.

Mistral’s answer, repeated across sessions, is a stack built on three pillars: open weights, model customization, and infrastructure independence. The pitch is that teams in regulated industries cannot use off-the-shelf AI. They need models fine-tuned on their own data, run on infrastructure they control, and customized for local languages and regulations.

The summit was the launch platform for several concrete announcements that moved Mistral from model provider to infrastructure operator. The most significant was Mistral Compute, a dedicated data center in Essonne scheduled to open in Q3 2026. The facility will house 18,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Superchips in a 40MW footprint.

- **Defense-specific deployment.** With both AMIAD director Bertrand Rondepierre and Mistral’s defense lead Nicolas Lourié on stage, the summit acknowledged that sovereign AI includes defense applications. The defense sessions focused on secure deployment architectures, air-gapped model serving, and the specific requirements of intelligence analysis and operational planning.

- Mistral’s first flagship summit, held in Paris on May 28, 2026, pivoted from model announcements to enterprise deployment, with three tracks covering strategy, engineering, and hands-on workshops.

candidates.title: Alan x Mistral: AI Health Hack

# Alan x Mistral: AI Health Hack
Alan
- **When** Saturday 11 April 2026 · 09:00–22:30 CEST
- **Where** [Paris](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=Paris%2C+%C3%8Ele-de-France)
- **Entry** Health
---
Join 30 of the sharpest AI builders from Paris and beyond for a day spent reimagining how the world stays healthy.
## **What to expect**
We’re bringing together the top **30 AI-native product builders** for 12 intense hours of building: one room, one track, one mission, to ship AI products that could change how people care for their health.
Whether it's a conversational health check-in, a preventive care nudge system, a mental wellness companion, or something no one has imagined yet, we want to see bold ideas that are AI-native and genuinely useful.
## **Why participate**
- Work alongside some of Paris’s best AI product builders, applying AI to one of the most consequential areas there is: health.
- Win prizes of up to **€2,500** for the top team
- Get free **Mistral Vibe credits** for the full day
- Enjoy breakfast, lunch, apéro, and post-event drinks, all on us
- Receive mentoring from Alan's engineering, product, and medical teams
## **Who we're looking for**
- Young professionals who love building things. Maybe you’ve launched a side project, started a company, built an internal tool at work, or put together something great at a previous hackathon
- Resourceful, curious people who know how to use AI to go from idea to prototype in a single day.
- People excited by health, not necessarily with healthcare experience, but with real curiosity about how AI can help people live healthier lives
- *No engineering background required*
**Spots are limited. Apply now to secure yours!**
**❗ Registrations close at midday on Thursday April 2nd.**
## **About the organisers:**
Alan is Europe's leading health partner, with a mission to **help people live in good health to 100**. Alan has built the one place where insurance, prevention, care access, and well-being services come together seamlessly in one app.
Mistral AI is a Paris-based company building some of the world's most powerful and efficient large language models. Mistral is on a mission to make frontier AI open, accessible, and European.

candidates.snippet:
Thales has reaffirmed its attractiveness by remaining in the number one position in the Universum ranking of the most attractive employers among engineering students in France for the second consecutive year. The Universum research institute covered 19,064 students, including 9,049 future engineers.

Supporting young people is a key focus of Thales’ HR policy. By 2026, the Group will offer nearly 3,300 internship and apprenticeship opportunities in France for students in higher education, as well as 1,500 internships for students in Year 10 and Year 11.
